Confirmed on the FLUX.1 VAE: RX 9060 XT (gfx1200), torch 2.12, Windows, bf16, 768-1536px, Invoke's ROCm SDPA guard installed, MIOPEN_FIND_MODE=FAST: implied 3451 decode / 2688 encode.

Peak reserved bytes per output pixel per element byte of the diffusers AutoencoderKL convolution stack. Fitted on the FLUX.2 VAE (the vae.flux2 cudnn points) with scripts/calibrate_flux2_working_memory.py --only vae: RTX 4090, torch 2.7.1, bf16, untiled, fused SDPA; implied 2180/2185/2165 decode and 1072/1063/1061 encode at 512/768/1024px, flat across resolution. Rounded up to 2200 / 1100, the pair the FLUX.1 estimator already shipped.

Peak reserved bytes per output pixel per element byte of the diffusers AutoencoderKL convolution stack on MIOpen. Fitted on the FLUX.2 VAE (the vae.flux2 miopen points) with scripts/calibrate_flux2_working_memory.py --only vae, torch 2.10, bf16, untiled: RX 9070 XT (gfx1201) implied 3453/3369/3368 decode, PRO W7900 (gfx1100) 3525 at 512px; encode 2687/2688/2688 on both cards, to the byte. Two AMD generations agreeing that closely make this MIOpen rather than a per-card quirk, so the values are the larger card's plus ~2% headroom: 3600 / 2750. MIOpen's convolution workspaces are larger than cuDNN's (~1.6x decode, ~2.4x encode), identically with fused and math attention, and its encode/decode ratio is 0.78 against cuDNN's 0.49.

scripts/calibrate_flux2_working_memory.py --only vae with SDPBackend.MATH forced on CUDA -- the regime MPS lands in; bf16, untiled; score_matrix_bytes is the full math-kernel score matrix. Forcing math measures below the fused path until 1536px. The 768px encode sits at the crossover, where the larger term alone is short and the device_working_mem_gb floor covers it; reproducible to three decimals across runs. Recorded in GiB.
